cases.name: uses print() rather than just writing text

exercise1.hint: Put your message inside print(), with the text in quotes: print("your message here").

cases.name: uses a separate print() for each line

exercise2.hint: Each line needs its own print() on its own line. Three lines of output means three print() statements.

choices: Sends the text to a printer
Writes the value to the output, so you can see it
Saves the value to a file
Stores the value in a variable
questions.explain: print() writes to standard output. The name is a leftover from when output really did go to a printer.

questions.prompt: Which of these will cause an error?
questions.explain: Without quotes, Python reads Hello as a variable name, and no variable by that name exists.

questions.prompt: How many lines does print("a")\nprint("b") produce?
questions.explain: Each print() ends with a newline, so each call starts its output on a fresh line.

questions.prompt: Why do single and double quotes both work for strings?
choices: Python accepts either, so you can use the other kind inside without escaping
questions.explain: Having both means you can write "it's fine" or 'she said "hi"' without escaping anything.
